avoid_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Chelation complex formation reduces levofloxacin absorption by 50-90%
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after levofloxacin

avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
avoid_supplements.action: Space dosing at least 2 hours apart; consider alternative timing

avoid_supplements.name: Iron supplements
avoid_supplements.action: Administer levofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after iron

avoid_supplements.name: Zinc supplements
avoid_supplements.action: Separate doses by at least 2 hours

avoid_supplements.name: Aluminum-containing antacids
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; space 2+ hours apart

caution_supplements.name: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May increase risk of CNS stimulation and seizure potential
caution_supplements.action: Use lowest effective dose; monitor for increased tremor or seizure risk

caution_supplements.name: Caffeine
caution_supplements.mechanism: Fluoroquinolones inhibit CYP1A2, potentially increasing caffeine levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for caffeine-related side effects; consider modest reduction

avoid_foods.name: Dairy products (milk, yogurt, cheese)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Calcium content chelates levofloxacin, reducing absorption
avoid_foods.action: Separate dairy intake by 2+ hours from levofloxacin dose

caution_foods.name: High-fiber foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May slightly reduce fluoroquinolone absorption if taken simultaneously
caution_foods.action: Space high-fiber meals by 1-2 hours from levofloxacin dosing

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods/beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Reduced CYP1A2 metabolism may elevate caffeine levels
caution_foods.action: Moderate caffeine intake during levofloxacin therapy

monitoring_notes: Levofloxacin is primarily renally excreted with minimal hepatic metabolism, making it relatively safe from CYP interactions but highly susceptible to chelation. Monitor for tendinopathy, QT prolongation, and CNS effects; counsel patients to take levofloxacin on an empty stomach separated from all divalent/trivalent cations and antacids.
